turns.t: G'day, doctor. It's my right elbow. Hurts on the outside. I've been painting the house, and I think I've done it. Um, what was I saying.
The outside of the right elbow. When did it start?
Last month? No, the month before. I painted the fence, then the shed. Not sure. ~
Is it there all the time, or only with certain things? ~
When I grip the brush. Or lift the kettle. Or shake hands, which is embarrassing.
Have you noticed any numbness or tingling in the fingers?
No numbness. No tingling.
Any neck pain?
No, the neck's fine.
What do you do for work?
I'm a painter. Which is the irony.
Any conditions I should know about?
Psoriasis. On my knees.
Let me feel the elbow. Tell me when you feel it.
There. Ow. ~
There's tenderness right over the bony bump on the outside of the elbow.
That's the spot. ~
Now hold your wrist up straight, and I'll push down on the back of your hand.
Like this? ~
Ah, yes. That reproduces the pain on the outside of the elbow when you resist.
That's the one. ~
Let me explain what's going on, without putting a name on it today. A tendon on the outside of the elbow takes the strain of gripping, and when it's overused, it gets sore and irritated. ~
So I've overdone it. ~
That's the picture. The tendon needs rest to recover. ~
I've got a job to finish. ~
I understand. Try to use the other hand for painting where you can, and take regular breaks.
I'm right-handed. ~
Switch for the heavy parts, or use a roller on an extension pole. ~
That's a good idea. ~
A tennis elbow strap, a band just below the elbow, can take the strain. You can buy one at the pharmacy.
Does it work? ~
It helps many people. Wear it when you're gripping. ~
Right. ~
Avoid lifting with your palm facing down. Lift with your palm facing up, it's gentler.
That's the opposite of what I do. ~
Try it. ~
I will. ~
If it's not better in six weeks, come back and we'll look at other options.
Six weeks. I'll write it on the fence. ~
Ha. Take care. ~
